selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What kinds of things did the king own that showed both wealth and knowledge?
questions.answer: He had precious treasure, hidden stores, advanced skills, wide learning, and deep knowledge in many fields.

questions.question: Why did the king want to open a public display?
questions.answer: He wanted his rule, riches, skill, and knowledge to become visible to others.

questions.question: What two ways did the king want his beauty and perfection to be seen?
questions.answer: He wanted to see them himself and also view them as reflected through other people.

questions.question: What is the main point of the comparison introduced to the listener?
questions.answer: It is meant to help explain the purpose of the world, why human beings were created, and the mystery connected to the prescribed prayers.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about someone who possesses beauty and excellence?
questions.answer: Such a person naturally wants those qualities to be seen and shown.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the mention of hidden treasures in addition to visible ones?
questions.answer: The king’s riches were even greater than what people normally saw.

questions.question: Why are both artistic skill and knowledge mentioned separately?
questions.answer: The passage presents the king as excellent not only in making things but also in understanding them deeply.

questions.question: How do the two stated “respects” help explain the purpose of the exhibition?
questions.answer: They show that the display had both a personal purpose for the king and a public purpose for the people.

questions.question: How does the list of the king’s possessions strengthen the comparison?
questions.answer: It builds a picture of complete greatness in material, intellectual, and artistic ways.

questions.question: What does the king possess besides jewels and precious stones?
questions.answer: He also has concealed treasures, remarkable skills, broad scientific knowledge, and deep learning.

questions.question: What moved the king to arrange an exhibition?
questions.answer: His wish to make his beauty and perfection known and visible.

questions.question: What parts of the king’s greatness were meant to appear before the people?
questions.answer: His authority, wealth, craftsmanship, and knowledge.

questions.question: According to the comparison, why is the king’s exhibition not random entertainment?
questions.answer: It has a clear purpose: to reveal what he has and who he is.

questions.question: What is the first way the king wanted to behold his perfection?
questions.answer: He wanted to observe it directly with his own awareness.

questions.question: What is the second way the king wanted to behold his perfection?
questions.answer: He wanted to see it through the perception of others.

questions.question: What does the passage imply about the connection between beauty and self-disclosure?
questions.answer: Real beauty tends toward being revealed rather than remaining hidden.

questions.question: What larger subjects is the listener being invited to understand through this example?
questions.answer: The meaning of the world’s purpose, the reason for human creation, and the mystery of prayer.

questions.question: What is the best summary of the king’s motive in the marked passage?
questions.answer: He wants his greatness and perfection to become known, witnessed, and appreciated.

questions.question: Who is directly addressed before the comparison begins, and what is he invited to do?
questions.answer: A “brother” is addressed and invited to reflect on a short example.

questions.question: What three major matters is this comparison supposed to help explain?
questions.answer: The purpose of the world, the creation of humanity, and the reality of the prescribed prayers.

questions.question: What does the king’s ownership of many treasures show about him?
questions.answer: It shows abundance, richness, and greatness.

questions.question: What does his mastery of unusual arts and sciences show in addition to wealth?
questions.answer: It shows refined ability and deep understanding.

questions.question: Why did the king want to put on displays for the people?
questions.answer: He wanted people to witness the signs of his splendor and excellence.

questions.question: In what sense was the exhibition also for the king himself?
questions.answer: It allowed him to contemplate his own perfection.

title: 11 Word Introduction to the Parable and the Sultan's Purpose
